answer: Lantern Draw Registration: each agent identity is admitted only by winning a slot in a beacon-derived random lottery, where the beacon value is revealed after registration closes so attackers cannot precompute favorable outcomes. Admission requires solving a per-slot verifiable delay puzzle, so each identity costs real sequential compute time, and an attacker submitting many identities pays that delay multiplied across every attempt. The meadow of candidates is sampled at a hidden horizon, meaning mass registration yields no statistical edge.
